title: B2 · L5 — wish + would
topic: Complaining about others' habits with wish + would
description: 'Wish + would' se usa para expresar molestia o queja sobre comportamientos habituales o irritantes de otras personas.

questions.prompt: Situación: te quejas a tu pareja por enésima vez.
questions.question: Complete: 'I wish you ___ leaving your clothes on the floor!'
options: stop
stopped
would stop
will stop
questions.explanation: 'Wish + would' se usa para quejarse de comportamientos ajenos molestos y recurrentes que queremos que cambien. Implica juicio y frustración. 'Wish + past' aquí sonaría a estado, no a acción irritante repetida. Regla clave: 'would' aporta la connotación 'por favor, deja de hacerlo YA'.
examples: I wish you would stop interrupting me every time I try to talk. → queja de pareja
I wish he would just listen for once instead of scrolling on his phone.

questions.statement: 'I wish it would rain' se puede usar para expresar un deseo sobre el clima.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Wish + would' también funciona con fenómenos no humanos (clima, tráfico, la conexión wifi, la economía) cuando algo persiste y queremos que cambie. Personifica ligeramente el fenómeno, como si tuviera voluntad. Muy común en quejas cotidianas y small talk sobre el tiempo.
examples: God, I wish it would stop snowing — I've shovelled the driveway three times today.
I wish the traffic would clear up. I've been in this jam for 40 minutes.

questions.prompt: Identifica el error gramatical más frecuente.
questions.question: Which is NOT possible in standard English?
options: I wish he would call me.
I wish I would be taller.
I wish they would arrive soon.
I wish she would stop complaining.
questions.explanation: Regla fundamental: 'wish + would' NUNCA se usa con el mismo sujeto ('I wish I would...' es agramatical). La razón lógica: 'would' expresa queja/deseo de cambio ajeno, y no tiene sentido quejarte de ti mismo con esa forma. Para deseos sobre uno mismo, usa 'wish + past' (estados) o 'wish + could' (habilidades).
examples: Incorrect: I wish I would be more disciplined. → error frecuente
Correct: I wish I were more disciplined / I wish I could be more disciplined.

questions.text: I wish my neighbours would turn down their music. It's driving me crazy.
questions.explanation: Connected speech: 'would turn' se enlaza con /d/ suave → 'wud-turn'. 'Turn down' se pronuncia como una sola unidad rítmica /tɜːn-daʊn/. 'It's driving me crazy' es una colocación idiomática fija — nunca 'making me crazy'. Nativos añaden intensidad con adverbios como 'absolutely' o 'literally' delante de 'driving me crazy'.
examples: I wish my flatmate would clean up after himself in the kitchen — it's absolutely disgusting.
I wish they would keep the noise down after 11 — some of us have to work in the morning.

questions.prompt: Comentas con un colega sobre alguien que siempre llega tarde a las reuniones.
questions.question: Choose the sentence expressing frustration with a repeated behaviour:
options: I wish he was more punctual.
I wish he would be more punctual.
I wish he had been punctual yesterday.
I wish he could be punctual.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + would' enfatiza el hartazgo por una conducta que se REPITE en el tiempo. 'Wish + past' (opción A) describiría un rasgo permanente sin la carga de queja. La opción C se refiere a un momento único pasado. La D sugiere que le falta capacidad, cosa que no es el caso.
examples: I wish he would arrive on time for once — just once! → hartazgo con toque irónico
I wish they would answer my emails within 24 hours. It's basic professionalism.

questions.statement: 'Wish + would' puede expresar a la vez crítica y deseo de cambio futuro.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Es una estructura de doble filo: critica el comportamiento presente e implica esperanza de cambio próximo. Por eso suena a queja constructiva más que a lamento pasivo. Muy útil en contextos laborales, familiares o cívicos donde queremos señalar un problema sin ser directamente confrontacionales.
examples: I wish my boss would appreciate my work more — I'm going the extra mile every week.
I wish the government would take real action on climate change instead of just talking.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada queja con su continuación natural:

pairs.right: warm up a bit — I'm freezing!

questions.explanation: Todos son quejas o deseos sobre agentes externos: personas, animales, objetos, fenómenos. La regla es sencilla: 'wish + would' se aplica a cualquier sujeto EXCEPTO uno mismo. Fíjate en la forma negativa: 'wouldn't + verbo' expresa deseo de que la acción negativa CESE.
examples: I wish you would stop shouting at the kids — it's not working. → intervención parental
I wish it would stop raining for five minutes so I can walk the dog.

questions.prompt: Un padre habla de su hijo adolescente.
questions.question: Which sentence expresses annoyance most clearly?
options: My son doesn't tidy his room.
My son doesn't like tidying his room.
I wish my son would tidy his room!
My son might tidy his room.
questions.explanation: 'I wish + would' añade una capa emocional que las simples afirmaciones no tienen: no sólo constata el hecho, sino que expresa frustración acumulada y demanda implícita de cambio. Las otras opciones son descriptivas o neutras, casi resignadas.
examples: I wish he would take some responsibility for once! → estallido parental controlado
I wish they would just apologise instead of doubling down every single time.

questions.target: I wish my colleagues would stop talking during meetings — it's really unprofessional.
questions.explanation: Queja laboral típica que se dice en confianza con un colega cercano, no delante de todo el equipo. Prosodia: da énfasis a 'stop' y a 'really' para transmitir el hartazgo. Nativos suavizan añadiendo hedging: 'Look, I don't want to be that person, but...' o 'Am I the only one who thinks...?'.
examples: Honestly, I wish my team would communicate more clearly on Slack. Half my day is spent chasing updates.
I really wish my manager would give proper feedback instead of just 'looks good'. It's not helpful.

questions.prompt: Llevas dos semanas queriendo salir a correr pero llueve.
questions.question: Complete: 'I wish it ___ raining. I want to go for a walk.'
options: stops
stopped
would stop
had stopped
questions.explanation: 'Wish + would' se usa con fenómenos climáticos persistentes que queremos que cesen. La forma 'stopped' (past) daría un matiz de estado hipotético menos natural aquí, y 'stops' es presente simple (agramatical tras wish). El matiz de 'would' es 'llevo tiempo esperando que pare'.
examples: God, I wish this heatwave would end — it's been over 40 degrees for a week.
I wish the wind would die down. My allergies are through the roof.

questions.statement: La diferencia entre 'I wish she were nicer' y 'I wish she would be nicer' es significativa.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Wish + past' ('were nicer') describe un rasgo de carácter percibido como estable o inmutable — casi resignación. 'Wish + would' ('would be nicer') critica su comportamiento actual e implica una demanda directa de cambio. El segundo suena más acusatorio, casi como reproche.
examples: I wish she were nicer. → constatación fatalista: 'así es ella, no cambia'
I wish she would be nicer. → reproche: 'podría esforzarse, pero elige no hacerlo'

questions.text: I wish people wouldn't chew with their mouth open. It's really off-putting.
questions.explanation: Queja social generalizada con 'people' (todos, en general). Connected speech: 'wouldn't chew' fusiona la /t/ silenciada → 'wudn(t)-chew'. 'Off-putting' /ˈɒf-pʊtɪŋ/ es adjetivo idiomático B2+ que significa 'desagradable, que da rechazo social'. Ojo: no confundir con 'putting off' (posponer).
examples: I wish people would use headphones on public transport — I don't need to hear TikTok at 8 a.m.
I wish people wouldn't be so rude in queues. Basic manners aren't that hard.

questions.prompt: Comentario en un artículo de opinión sobre políticas públicas.
questions.question: Choose the most natural complaint about institutions:
options: I wish the government does something.
I wish the government would do something.
I wish the government to do something.
I wish the government did something last year.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + would' es la fórmula estándar para exigir acción a instituciones, autoridades o entidades abstractas (empresa, sistema, sociedad). Es la voz del ciudadano/consumidor frustrado, típica en editoriales, discurso político y periodismo de opinión. Suena a crítica activa, no a resignación.
examples: I wish the council would fix the potholes on Main Street — they've been there for months.
I wish schools would teach basic financial literacy. Kids leave clueless about mortgages.

questions.target: I wish my brother would return the books he borrowed. He's had them for months.
questions.explanation: Queja familiar cotidiana con tono de leve exasperación, no de ira. Prosodia: énfasis en 'return' y en 'months' — la palabra que justifica el hartazgo. Nativos suavizan añadiendo humor: 'I'm starting to think he sold them' o 'at this point they're his books'.
examples: I wish my friend would just reply to my messages. It's been three days for a yes-or-no question.
Honestly, I wish my flatmate would clean the kitchen once in a while. It's not that hard.

questions.prompt: Identifica cuál viola la regla de sujeto de 'wish + would'.
questions.question: Which sentence CANNOT use 'would'?
options: I wish it ___ stop snowing.
I wish you ___ listen to me.
I wish I ___ know the answer.
I wish they ___ arrive.
questions.explanation: 'I wish I would' es agramatical: 'wish + would' NUNCA lleva el mismo sujeto (I...I). La forma correcta para deseos sobre uno mismo con verbos de estado (know, be, have) es 'wish + past simple': 'I wish I KNEW the answer'. Este error es el más frecuente en exámenes B2 First.
examples: Correct: I wish I knew the answer to that pub quiz question.
Incorrect: I wish I would know the answer. → error clásico, evítalo siempre
